correctness.rationale: Character orthogonality gives q^(-4) times the squared triple-fiber norm with the stated counting measure, so the unnormalized coefficient is q+1−1/q. For each nonzero sum s there are q translation orbits of ordered triples and translating by h changes the square sum by −hs; each orbit contributes exactly once to every square sum. Thus the generic fibers have size q. At s=0, the unique ordered parametrization (a−d,a,a+d) gives square sum −d². The d=0 fiber has size q and the nonempty nonzero-square-sum fibers have size 2q; C_d=C_{−d} gives |C_0|²+2Σ_{d≠0}|C_d|². After spending one q-term Cauchy–Schwarz estimate per d against the exceptional contribution excluded from the generic estimate, the remainder is Σ_{d≠0}|C_d|². Cauchy–Schwarz against the central factor and the bijection (a,d)↦(a−d,a+d) bound this by F(F²−Σ|f|⁴). The last Cauchy–Schwarz bound is sharp only for constant modulus when F>0. Independently counting the flat moment gives q⁴+q³−q², yielding 99, 7209 and 550395 at q=3,9,27, respectively. Quadratic phases translate (X,Y), preserving the norm. There is no claim of a full equality-phase classification. The reviewed verify.py (arithmetic and fiber enumeration, lines 12–56; test chain, lines 58–104) and verify_output.txt corroborate the finite cases; the complex sample tests use tolerances, and neither they nor the recorded run are used as proof. Replay: python verify.py from the package; not executed as part of this review.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct contribution is the unrestricted characteristic-three theorem for extension fields q≥9. The q=3 case itself is covered by an earlier three-mode result, and the identical coefficient and necessary modulus condition are known in characteristic >3. The frozen text explicitly distinguishes both overlaps; no inspected result establishes the unrestricted theorem on the remaining fields.
residual_risks: Best-of-knowledge coverage judgment; an unindexed characteristic-three sharp inequality or equivalent weighted-energy inequality could exist. A broad lookup without returned evidence does not exclude this.

value.rationale: The result fills the explicit exceptional-characteristic gap in a sharp parabola restriction problem, on arbitrarily large fields and for every complex input. It explains how to recover the sharp coefficient despite the factor-two critical fibers and gives necessary optimizer structure. This is materially stronger than tabulating the flat energy or testing local stability.
